## Summary

Isopentyl acetate (3-methylbutyl acetate, "banana oil") by Fischer
esterification of isopentyl alcohol with an excess of glacial acetic acid
and a sulfuric acid catalyst, followed by an aqueous workup and simple
distillation. This is sample data: the quantities follow the textbook
method but are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Isopentyl alcohol (3-methylbutan-1-ol) | 123-51-3 | 88.15 | 4.41 g (5.44 mL) | 50.0 | 1.0 |
| Acetic acid, glacial | 64-19-7 | 60.05 | 6.01 g (5.73 mL) | 100 | 2.0 |
| Sulfuric acid, 96 % | 7664-93-9 | 98.08 | 0.5 mL | cat. | cat. |

## Procedure

1. Place the isopentyl alcohol (4.41 g, 5.44 mL, 50.0 mmol) and the
   glacial acetic acid (6.01 g, 5.73 mL, 100 mmol) in a 50 mL
   round-bottomed flask containing a magnetic stirring bar and two
   boiling chips.
2. In a fume hood, add the concentrated sulfuric acid (0.5 mL) dropwise
   from a Pasteur pipette while swirling the flask (Note 1).
3. Fit a water-cooled reflux condenser and heat the mixture under gentle
   reflux on a heating mantle for 60 minutes.
4. Let the flask cool to room temperature. The fruity odour of the ester
   is now unmistakable, reminiscent of ripe bananas.
5. Pour the cooled mixture into a separatory funnel containing cold water
   (25 mL), rinsing the flask with a further 5 mL of water.

## Workup and Purification

Shake the funnel, let the layers separate and discard the lower aqueous
layer. Wash the upper ester layer with saturated aqueous sodium hydrogen
carbonate in two 15 mL portions, swirling before stoppering and venting
often because carbon dioxide is evolved (Note 2), until the washings are
no longer acidic. Wash the ester once with saturated sodium chloride
solution (10 mL), transfer it to a small conical flask and dry it over
anhydrous sodium sulfate for 10 minutes. Decant it into a dry 25 mL
flask and distil it at atmospheric pressure, collecting the fraction
that distils at a constant temperature. Expected yield 4.56 g
(35.0 mmol, 70 %).

## Characterization

Colourless liquid with a strong banana-like odour. Record the boiling
range of the collected fraction. The IR spectrum (neat film) shows the
ester C=O stretch near 1740 cm⁻¹ and no broad O–H band of the alcohol.
Expected ¹H NMR signals (CDCl₃): δ 4.09 (t, 2H, OCH₂), 2.04 (s, 3H,
COCH₃), 1.68 (m, 1H, CH), 1.51 (q, 2H, CH₂), 0.92 (d, 6H, 2 × CH₃).

## Notes

1. Mixing sulfuric acid with the organic reagents releases heat; add it
   slowly.
2. The hydrogen carbonate wash removes the excess acetic acid and the
   sulfuric acid. Vent the funnel after every few shakes.
3. The esterification is an equilibrium. The two-fold excess of acetic
   acid pushes it towards the ester; the excess is removed in the
   aqueous washes.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Isopentyl alcohol and the product are flammable liquids; keep them away
from flames and hot surfaces. Isopentyl alcohol is harmful if inhaled
and irritates skin and eyes. Glacial acetic acid and concentrated
sulfuric acid cause severe burns to skin and eyes; wear gloves and eye
protection and handle both in a fume hood. Neutralise the combined
aqueous washes and dispose of them as aqueous waste. Collect the
distillation residue as non-halogenated organic waste.

## References

1. Furniss, B. S.; Hannaford, A. J.; Smith, P. W. G.; Tatchell, A. R.
